semanticText:
# Activation Clause

Activation Clause maintains a document’s party roster, acceptance boundary and access guard. It separates agreement to terms from permission to read participant timelines and authority to perform operations. Its executable hooks come from its admitted exact type. Hosted bootstrap resolves account locators into authenticated transports before initialization.

## Configuration

`parameters.parties` must be a nonempty object. Each party needs `lead.channel`; optional `representatives` supply additional channels. Party and representative keys must be nonempty text without `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`. Lead channels use the party key; representative channels use `party__representative`. Party and business descriptions identify participants but do not prove authority.

`required` defaults to all configured party keys. `revision` defaults to 1, `allowNewParties` to false, and `readers`, `accessPaths`, `preActivationOperations` and `preActivationChannels` to empty collections. `frozen` defaults to false but is also enabled when the document’s `partyRosterFrozen` is true. These are initialization defaults, not meanings of missing runtime state.

`accessPaths` identifies embedded Timeline Access documents. `readers` supplies additional groups of alternative reader keys; party `readerKeys` and representative `readerKeys` add groups under their transport names, replacing same-named groups. For each Timeline Channel transport, one matching access document must include its exact timeline, match its provider, and contain at least one key from every reader group. Empty groups cannot satisfy this check. Transports recognized as External Channel are exempt from this matching requirement.

`negotiation.allowedPaths` defaults to empty. Nonempty configuration enables negotiation for the required approvers and requires a typed target document. Paths must be distinct absolute paths without empty segments or `~`, cannot target executable/control roots (`clauses`, `contracts`, `activation`, `clauseRuntime`, `type`, `name`, `description`), and cannot equal or descend from an `accessPaths` entry. Selected fields must exist and be scalar text, integer, double or boolean.

## Acceptance and lifecycle

Initialization and completed embedded `Timeline Access Updated` deliveries refresh activation. Runtime state is stored in `/activation`. `approved` records party acceptance; `termsAccepted` requires every `required` party’s approval and agreement between live negotiated fields and the recorded terms. `accessReady` and `functional` record the access check, including proposed parties in admission requests matching the current revision. `active` additionally requires that the document is not `closed`.

`status` is `CLOSED` when closed; otherwise missing confirmed access yields `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS` before first activation or `SUSPENDED_ACCESS` afterward. With access available, it is `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE` until acceptance is complete, then `ACTIVE`. `reason` identifies `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`, `ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED`, or no such deficit. `everActivated` preserves the distinction between never activated and subsequently suspended.

`approve_<party>` requires the party’s lead channel, exact-document review, the current `revision`, and valid participant access. When negotiation is enabled, it also requires the current `termsRef`. Repeated acceptance is a no-op; a new acceptance emits `Terms Accepted`. Acceptance alone does not establish activation. Committed transitions emit `Document Activated` on first activation, `Document Access Suspended` when an active document loses access, and `Document Access Restored` when it becomes active again after an access deficit.

The dispatch guard permits initialization and registered embedded access updates to proceed even while business delivery is blocked. Other deliveries require initialized state, available access and an open document. Configured pre-activation operations and non-external channels can then proceed before acceptance; ordinary business delivery requires acceptance of current terms. Registered admission-consent operations have a separate exception requiring an exact pending admission, matching revision, token, operation and lead-channel identities. A denied external delivery is consumed and checkpointed, not queued for automatic replay.

## Party changes and admission

`updateParty_<party>` requires exact-document review, an unfrozen roster and an invoking party lead. Input `party` defaults to that invoking party; an existing different party cannot be managed. Adding a party requires `allowNewParties` and an explicit new key. `replacement` needs `lead.channel`, valid representative names and access coverage for the resulting roster. A successful update installs the roster’s contracts, clears approvals, increments `revision`, and adds a newly created party to `required`.

Approved admission is separate: it requires a configured nonempty `admission.approvers`, the expected revision, an unfrozen roster, compatible main identities and access coverage. It does not itself append new required approvers or supply participant consent. `Party Addition Requested` can install validated public access histories and emit transport-specific `Party Access Update Requested` events. These request provider-owned permission changes; they do not grant access. Stale requests and already-recorded admission references are ignored. Installed histories must retain the native Timeline Access executable policy and initialization/checkpoint evidence; installation accepts 1–16 documents per call and deduplicates by original document identity.

## Negotiation

`terms.ref` identifies the recorded definition and selected field values; `termsRevision` starts at 1. Negotiation operations require exact-document review and a channel in `required`.

`proposeChanges` requires current `baseTermsRef`, a nonempty `changes` list and an unused `proposalId`. Each change contains an allowed `path` and `replacement` of the same scalar kind; the complete candidate must satisfy the document type. Duplicate paths and unchanged terms are rejected. Proposal identifiers must be nonempty and contain neither `/` nor `~`. Reusing a pending identifier requires identical content; replacing another pending proposal requires its identifier in `supersedes`.

`activate` selects current terms with `termsRef` and no `proposalId`, or proposed terms with both matching references. Proposed terms are revalidated before approval. Only all required proposal approvals apply the replacement fields, advance activation, terms and negotiation revisions, transfer approvals, and record `APPLIED`. `proposeAndActivate` combines proposal creation with the caller’s approval; it does not guarantee unanimous acceptance.

Before first activation, required approvers may withdraw their own acceptance or reject a proposal; only its proposer may withdraw the proposal itself. Recorded proposal outcomes distinguish `APPLIED`, `REJECTED`, `WITHDRAWN`, `SUPERSEDED` and `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`. Applying negotiated terms freezes negotiation editing; activation on current terms also freezes it and supersedes a pending proposal. Roster or required-approver changes replace the terms identity, clear pending proposals, advance `termsRevision`, and clear approvals when negotiation is enabled. Clause transitions cannot bypass these party operations; before first activation, enabled negotiation also locks changes to the clause configuration set.

Access notifications and emitted requests are not substitutes for confirmed, executed permission history. Read access, roster membership and callable operations do not by themselves establish consent, personal obligation or permission for a particular viewer.
